angle: exp is the fixed point of differentiation stated as motion (z' = k z); aiming the complex rate k from the real axis to the imaginary axis turns growth into rotation, so Euler's formula is kinematics — a perpendicular push cannot change |z|, unit speed makes arc = angle = time, and e^{iπ} = -1 just means half a turn

libraries.name: Two.js
libraries.role: retained-mode 2D scene graph for all seven complex-plane scenes (hero triptych, real-line law, scale-and-turn dial, the k-plane/z-plane centrepiece, the perpendicularity scene with its |z(t)| strip chart, the series arrow chain, the Euler-vs-RK4 comparison); trails, arrowheads, dashed unit circles, dynamic grids and tick labels are persistent objects whose vertices are mutated each frame

libraries.name: Three.js
libraries.role: the 3D helix payoff: the curve (t, cos t, sin t) drawn as a BufferGeometry line with three projected shadows (cosine wave on the floor plane, sine wave on the wall plane, unit circle down the time axis), plus synced marker spheres and drop lines

libraries.name: OrbitControls
libraries.role: globalised THREE.OrbitControls for free-orbit dragging of the helix; pulled from r147 because examples/js was removed in r148, and it is API-compatible with the r149 core

libraries.name: anime.js
libraries.role: short user-initiated transitions: tweening the complex rate k to a preset, scrubbing theta to the pi/2, pi, 3pi/2, 2pi landmarks, easing a back to exactly zero, and the 900ms camera position + up-vector + field-of-view flights between the three locked helix viewpoints

libraries.name: KaTeX
libraries.role: every mathematical statement on screen, rendered from data-tex / data-tex-display attributes at boot; inline in prose, captions, legends and readout labels, display mode for the staged argument

building_blocks: complex-arithmetic-module: cadd/cmul/cscale/cabs/carg/cexp on {re,im} plain objects, ~30 lines, no library
View: bidirectional math<->pixel mapping object (X(re), Y(im), re(px), im(py)) with mutable centre and scale

Grid: reusable dynamic axis component — nice-number tick stepping (1/2/2.5/5/10 decade ladder targeting 46px spacing), preallocated grid lines, axis lines, tick labels, optional dashed unit circle, all repositioned per frame from a View
Arrow: two-part Two.js primitive (line + filled triangle head) with .set(x0,y0,x1,y1), auto-hide below a pixel-length threshold, runtime recolour and width
preallocated-polyline: fixed-vertex-count Two.Path whose anchors are rewritten each frame (trail, ghost/future path, arc gauge, integrator tracks), with unused vertices collapsed onto the last point
rAF-driver-with-IntersectionObserver-gating: one global animation loop; each registered scene renders only while its host element is near the viewport
responsive-fixed-logical-canvas: canvas sized in logical units, CSS-scaled to 100% width with height:auto, plus a pointer-event mapper that rescales clientX/Y by (logicalW / rect.width)
draggable-complex-handle: pointerdown/move/up with pointer capture, magnitude clamping to a disc, and cancellation of any in-flight tween on user grab
dual-plane-layout: parameter plane (rate k) and state plane (motion z) side by side, the first driving the second live
auto-fit-view: smoothed (lerped) scale that frames only the travelled portion of the trajectory, so zooming out is itself the visualisation of growth
velocity-decomposition-overlay: velocity arrow drawn first and thick, its radial and tangential components drawn thinner on top so a vanishing component reads as a coloured core
right-angle-marker: 3-vertex corner path built from the unit position vector and its 90deg rotation
strip-chart: small in-canvas time series (|z(t)| vs t) with a reference line, moving head marker and adaptive vertical range
series-arrow-chain: head-to-tail vector sum of series terms with cumulative-sum anchors, per-term parity tinting, and a residual line to the exact value
landmark-buttons: named parameter values (pi/2, pi, 3pi/2, 2pi) that ease the scrubber there and pop an in-canvas badge on arrival
integrator-comparison-scene: same ODE stepped by two methods plus the closed form, drawn in one view with a live error table

orthographic-ish-locked-camera: far camera distance with a field of view computed from the content half-extents and the live aspect ratio, so a locked 3D view is effectively an orthographic projection
camera-seat-tween: anime.js tween over position + up vector + fov with controls disabled during flight and re-enabled only for the free seat
katex-attribute-renderer: data-tex / data-tex-display sweep at boot with per-node try/catch fallback to raw text
overflow-safe-display-math: .tex-block wrappers with overflow-x:auto, and \begin{aligned} rewrites for equations too wide for a panel
readout-table: label/value rows with tabular-nums, colour swatches keyed to the on-canvas semantics
staged-scroll-narrative: vertical fold-down sections, each one beat, with left/right splits for figure-vs-algebra
honesty-callout: styled caveat blocks that name the exact hypothesis being spent (absolute convergence, definition-not-repeated-multiplication, exact-vs-integrated)
computations: exact solution z(t) = e^{kt} for complex k, evaluated as e^{at}(cos bt + i sin bt) at every frame for the hero, §01, §03, §04 and §06
velocity z' = k·z by complex multiplication, and its split into the radial part (Re k)·z and the tangential part (Im k)·(i z)
d|z|/dt = (Re k)·|z|, shown live and going to exactly 0 when Re k = 0
arc length swept = ∫|z'|dt = |k|·(e^{at} − 1)/a, with the a → 0 limit |k|·t handled separately
|z| and arg z tracked against the closed forms e^{at} and b·t
cos t + i sin t computed independently and displayed alongside z(t) for comparison at every t
complex exponential series Σ (iθ)^n/n! generated by the recurrence v_n = v_{n-1}·(iθ/n), summed head to tail, with cumulative partial sums
residual |S_N − e^{iθ}| and |S_N|, compared against the first omitted term (5.34e−10 vs π^21/21! ≈ 5.7e−10 at θ=π, N=20)
longest term magnitude θ^n/n! over the visible chain
forward Euler stepping of z' = iz: z_{n+1} = z_n(1 + ih), with the closed-form radius (1+h²)^{N/2} shown for comparison
classical RK4 stepping of z' = iz with the four-stage increment, whose modulus matches (1 − h⁶/72 + h⁸/576)^{N/2}
per-frame |z| drift of both integrators against the exact value 1
nice-number axis tick stepping from a 1/2/2.5/5/10 decade ladder against a target pixel spacing
auto-fit view scale from the max |Re| and |Im| over 41 samples of the travelled trajectory
camera field of view solved from content half-extents, viewport aspect and camera distance so a locked 3D view is effectively orthographic
cos²t + sin²t displayed to six decimals as the coordinate form of |e^{it}| = 1
interactions: §02: drag the violet k arrow or the blue z arrow anywhere in the plane; both arg-k arcs, the k·z arrow, |k|, arg k and k·z update live
§03: drag the rate k anywhere in the k-plane and the entire trajectory in the z-plane re-solves every frame — the one gesture that morphs a ray continuously into a spiral and then a circle
§03: seven preset rates (growth, decay, circle, 2i, spiral out, spiral in, zero) tweened into place
§03: time scrubber over [0, 2π], play/pause, auto-zoom toggle, split-velocity toggle
§04: slide a = Re k across zero and watch the flat |z(t)| line bend and the pink radial arrow wake up; 'snap a → 0' eases it back to exactly zero
§04: time scrubber plus four landmark buttons (π/2, π, 3π/2, 2π) that ease the clock there and badge the arrival value (i, −1, −i, 1)
§05: θ slider, N (number of terms) slider, three θ presets, and an 'add terms' animation that grows the chain term by term
§05: parity tint toggle separating the real (even) and imaginary (odd) terms
§06: drag to orbit and scroll to zoom the helix; four camera seats (free, down the t-axis → circle, side → cos t, other side → sin t) flown by tween
§06: time scrubber along the helix, play/pause, and a toggle for the drop lines connecting the particle to its three shadows
§07: step-count slider N from 6 to 200, redrawing the Euler and RK4 tracks and recomputing both final radii and their errors
assets: katex.min.css with its .woff and .ttf src fallbacks stripped so only the vendored .woff2 files are ever requested
gotchas: anime.js v3 sets suspendWhenDocumentHidden = true and refuses to start its rAF engine while document.hidden — every transition silently freezes in a background tab (and in headless rendering). Fixed with anime.suspendWhenDocumentHidden = false at boot.

Three.js removed examples/js in r148, so there is no globalised OrbitControls shipped with r149. Vendored the r147 examples/js build, which is API-compatible with the r149 core. ES-module builds plus importmaps fail outright from file:// (CORS origin null).

Two.js makePath() calls center() on the path it creates, translating the vertices out from under you. Constructed new Two.Path(anchors, closed, curved) and two.add() instead so vertices stay in absolute pixel space.
Two.Anchor defaults its command to 'M'; Two.Path fixes the commands to M,L,L,... on _update only while automatic is true — safe here, but a manual path needs commands set explicitly.
KaTeX refuses to render in quirks mode, so the file must start with <!DOCTYPE html>.
katex.min.css lists .woff2, .woff and .ttf sources per face; vendoring only .woff2 leaves two 404s per font offline. Stripped the fallback src entries with a regex.
Whitespace-only text nodes between inline-flex children are not rendered as flex items, which glued legend labels to their adjacent KaTeX spans. Fixed with gap on the flex container.
KaTeX display math does not wrap; long equations overflowed their panels. Wrapped every .tex-block/.big-tex in overflow-x:auto and rebuilt the two widest with \begin{aligned}.
Two.js canvases are sized in logical units, so pointer coordinates must be rescaled by (logicalWidth / boundingRect.width) once the canvas is CSS-scaled to 100% width.

Auto-fitting the §03 view to the whole time window collapses the unit circle to sub-pixel size for k = 1 (e^{2π} ≈ 535). Fitting only the travelled arc keeps the frame usable and makes the zoom-out itself read as growth.

Three.js locked camera views need their up-vectors chosen deliberately: the naive (0,1,0) for a +y camera renders the sine wave upside-down and puts cos on the vertical axis of the circle view, contradicting §04's Re/Im convention.

requestAnimationFrame is unreliable under Chrome's --virtual-time-budget, so anime.js-driven transitions cannot be verified with --dump-dom screenshots; they were verified over the DevTools protocol in real time instead.
